title: Nervous system & reflex arc
examples: What is the difference between a reflex and a conscious action?
Can you explain the path a signal takes in a reflex?
How fast is the reflex arc compared to thinking about it?

explain.say: A receptor is the first part that detects a change in the body.
Now let me show you the real thing in 3D: a nerve cell. Look at the dendrites, the cell body and the nucleus. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.
The nerve transmits the message from the receptor to the central nervous system.
The central nervous system processes the information and sends an instruction back out.
An effector is the muscle or gland that carries out the response to the stimulus.
A reflex arc shows the whole pathway from detection to action quickly.
When you quickly pull your hand from something hot, that is a reflex arc in action.

faq.q: What is the difference between a reflex and a conscious action?
faq.a: A reflex is an automatic, rapid response that does not require thinking. You might also ask if it bypasses the brain, or if it is involuntary.
asks: Does a reflex need the brain to work?

faq.q: Does the signal always go to the brain first?
faq.a: No, in a simple reflex, the signal often goes to the spinal cord first. You could also ask if the spinal cord handles the message, or if the brain is skipped.
asks: Does the signal go to the brain first?
Can the reflex happen without the brain?

faq.q: What kind of receptors are in our skin?
faq.a: Our skin has many receptors that detect things like heat, pressure, and pain. You might ask about touch receptors, or pain receptors.
asks: What receptors are in the skin?

faq.q: What is the role of the effector in this process?
faq.a: The effector is the muscle or gland that actually does the work. It is the part that moves or secretes something. You could ask what carries out the response, or what is the final action.
asks: Which part responds to the signal?

faq.q: How fast is the reflex arc compared to thinking about it?
faq.a: A reflex arc is much faster because it uses a direct pathway through the spinal cord. You could ask about reaction time, or if it is instantaneous.

facts: Receptors detect changes, or stimuli, in the internal or external environment.
The nerve transmits the electrical impulse from the receptor.
The central nervous system processes the information rapidly.
Effectors are muscles or glands that produce the physical response.

quiz.say: When you touch a hot stove, which part detects the heat?
quiz.why: The receptor is the specialized cell that detects the change, like heat.

wrong.0: The effector is the muscle that moves, it does not detect the heat.
wrong.1: The spinal cord processes the message, but the detection starts at the receptor.
wrong.3: The nerve only carries the message, it does not detect the heat itself.

quiz.say: If a signal travels from the spinal cord to the arm muscle, what is the muscle acting as?
quiz.why: The effector is the muscle that carries out the physical action of pulling the hand away.

wrong.0: The nerve is the wire that carries the signal, not the thing that moves.
wrong.1: The CNS processes the signal, but the effector is the final responding part.
wrong.3: The receptor only detects the initial stimulus, it does not move.

quiz.say: The pathway from stimulus to response is best described as a:
quiz.why: The reflex arc names the entire pathway, from the starting detection to the final action.

wrong.1: Pathway is too general; reflex arc is the specific biological term.
wrong.2: A cycle suggests repetition, but this is a single, immediate response.
wrong.3: A circuit usually refers to electrical components, not biological pathways.
